items.title: Why Is Oracle Stock Down Today?
items.summary: Oracle spent $23.7 billion more cash than it brought in last fiscal year and borrowed $43 billion to cover the gap. That's a fine trade when money is cheap. It's a worse one with the 30-year Treasury yield near a 20-year high and long bonds selling off from Tokyo to London.

items.summary: SMRs could make it much easier to deploy nuclear power plants.

items.title: Apple Rises 3% on John Ternus’s First Day as CEO Even While the NASDAQ Skids
items.summary: John Ternus stepped into the CEO role at Apple on a day when rising Treasury yields cracked the AI infrastructure trade wide open, and the reason Apple surged while Oracle cratered reveals a structural fault line forming beneath the entire technology sector.

items.title: Oracle Falls 4% as Bond Selloff Tests Its Debt-Funded AI Buildout, Nebius Slips
items.summary: Rising Treasury yields are hitting debt-heavy AI builders where it hurts most, and Oracle's balance sheet puts it squarely in the crosshairs. Here is what the bond market is saying about the cost of building the AI future.

items.title: Why Oracle (ORCL) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

items.title: AI Is Coming for One of Legacy Software’s Most Defensible Businesses as a New Challenger Takes on Oracle, SAP and Workday
items.summary: Swapping out an ERP system has been compared to open-heart surgery, which is exactly why Oracle, SAP, and Workday have held their ground through every technology wave. Now an AI-native startup backed by a former Sequoia partner is betting that a rebuilt architecture can finally make the pain worth it.
